findings.title: Supplying a dummy totpCode skips password verification for backup-code login
findings.body: Password verification only runs when credentials.totpCode is empty (line 121), but the new backup-code branch at line 131 runs whenever credentials.backupCode is present regardless of totpCode. A direct credentials request containing a valid backupCode plus any non-empty totpCode value therefore skips password verification entirely and never validates the dummy TOTP, so a stolen backup code alone becomes a single-factor full login credential instead of a second factor after the password.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write and allows parallel reuse
findings.body: The code reads and decrypts the backup-code array, checks indexOf, then writes back the array with that entry nulled (lines 139-156) with no transaction, conditional update, or locking. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both pass the index check before either update commits, so a code advertised as usable exactly once can be replayed in parallel sessions.

findings.title: Backup codes are unreachable for Google/SAML users in the external TOTP flow
findings.body: Authorize throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled whenever identityProvider is not CAL and credentials.totpCode is empty (line 113). Users redirected from Google/SAML via loginWithTotp who choose 'Lost access' submit a backupCode with an empty totpCode, so they are rejected before the new backup-code branch at line 131 is ever reached, making backup-code recovery unusable for non-CAL 2FA users.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and only strips dashes
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex in setup.ts, but login (line 144) and the disable endpoint only remove '-' characters before an exact indexOf match. A user who types the code in uppercase (as suggested by the 'XXXXX-XXXXX' placeholder) or with surrounding spaces will be told the code is incorrect even though they entered the right code, and may burn attempts or get locked out of recovery.

findings.title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: Setup rejects any user with twoFactorEnabled=true with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled (lines 42-44), and no other endpoint or UI in this PR generates or regenerates backup codes. Existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes=null, get MissingBackupCodes at login/disable, and are told by the new 'missing_backup_codes' message to generate them in settings, which is impossible without fully disabling and re-enabling 2FA.
